title: Word Break II
prompt:
Given a string `s` and a dictionary of strings `wordDict`, add spaces in `s` to construct a sentence where each word is a valid dictionary word. Return all such possible sentences.

Note that the same word in `wordDict` may be reused multiple times when segmenting.

For deterministic comparison, sort the resulting list of sentences.

examples.explanation: Both segmentations use only dictionary words and cover the whole string.

constraints: s and wordDict[i] consist of only lowercase English letters
All strings in wordDict are unique
hints: This is Word Break, but instead of a yes/no answer you need every valid segmentation — backtrack over cut positions, branching into every dictionary word that matches a prefix of the remaining string.
Many different starting positions will end up re-exploring segmentations of the same suffix of s — memoize the list of valid sentences for each starting index to avoid exponential blowup.
Put wordDict into a set for O(1) membership checks. At each position, try every prefix length up to the longest dictionary word, and only recurse into a prefix that is itself a dictionary word.

solution.approach: Put wordDict into a set for O(1) lookups. Define a memoized recursive function break_from(start) that returns the list of all valid sentences for the suffix s[start:]. Base case: start == len(s) returns [''] (one empty continuation). Otherwise, try every end position from start+1 to len(s): if s[start:end] is a dictionary word, recursively get all sentences for the remainder s[end:], and for each, prepend the current word (with a space if the remainder is non-empty) to form a full sentence for this suffix. Memoizing on start is what keeps this efficient, since without it, common suffixes get re-segmented repeatedly across different backtracking branches, causing exponential blowup even though there are only O(n) distinct suffixes.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n^2) distinct suffix states times O(n) work per state, plus O(k) to build the k output sentences
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n * k) for memoized sentence lists, where k is the number of segmentations of a suffix
